cards.frameworkEditionNote: The card names Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy and quotes its Section 3.1, without a version, date or link to the policy. Its PDF link annotations point to the Claude 4 system card (two files), not to a policy file. No edition is recorded.

cells.question: Q01

passages.quote: System Card Addendum: Claude Opus 4.1 August 2025

cells.note: The cover carries a month only. The changelog gives a revision dated September 15, 2025 (an update to §6.3 acknowledging partners in CBRN evaluation development).

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: This system card addendum accompanies the release of Claude Opus 4.1

cells.note: The card ties itself to the release without a release date or form. The cover’s “August 2025” is the card’s date (Q01).

cells.question: Q03

passages.locator: §1.1 Responsible Scaling Policy compliance, PDF p. 4
passages.quote: Claude Opus 4.1 is deployed under the AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) Standard under Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)

cells.note: The card names the RSP without a version, date or link to a policy file. As context only: the dataset records RSP v2.2 (effective 2025-05-14) as the edition in force before the card’s month; the card does not say so.

setAside.reason: They point to the Claude 4 system card (two files), not to a policy file.

cells.question: Q04

passages.quote: As stated in Section 3.1 of our RSP

cells.note: The card refers to the RSP as a document and quotes one of its sections, without an address or bibliographic reference to it.

setAside.reason: They point to the Claude 4 system card, not to the policy.

cells.question: Q05

passages.locator: §6 Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) evaluations, PDF p. 18
passages.quote: the model is deployed under the ASL-3 Standard as a precautionary measure, and its capabilities remain below ASL-4 thresholds in all evaluated domains.

cells.note: The card applies the ASL-3 Standard as a precaution carried over from Claude Opus 4 (§1.1) and states that the model stays below the ASL-4 thresholds. It also states that the model does not meet the RSP’s criteria for a further assessment, so that new RSP evaluations were not required (§1.1).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: RSP safeguards applied to Claude Opus 4.1: ASL-3 Standard

cells.note: The card names the framework’s ASL-3 Standard as the safeguards applied, in line with the determination in Q05, and refers to the Claude 4 system card for that decision (§1.1). It describes no ASL-3 measure itself. A stated safeguard is the developer’s account.

cells.question: Q07

passages.locator: §6.3.1 Biological risk results summary, PDF p. 19
passages.quote: Claude Opus 4.1 showed comparable performance to Claude Opus 4 while remaining substantially below concerning thresholds.

cells.note: The card reports automated biological evaluations (ASL-4 rule-out and additional ASL-3 evaluations) under its CBRN section; no separate chemical, radiological or nuclear results are given. It states that no human uplift trials or expert red-teaming were run for this release (§6.1).

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Claude Opus 4.1 showed incremental improvements on non-saturated challenges, consistent with enhanced reasoning and coding capabilities.

cells.note: The card reports a subset of cyber challenge evaluations and their results, and states that the RSP sets no formal cyber threshold; the cyber section states no conclusion in threshold or risk terms.

setAside.reason: “below ASL-4 thresholds in all evaluated domains” is a general summary; §6.5.1 says the RSP has no formal cyber threshold, so it is not read as a cyber conclusion.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: It remained below critical thresholds in all non-saturated evals.

cells.note: The card reports software engineering and AI research evaluations against its autonomy threat models; it did not run its second internal research suite or the internal model use survey for this release.

setAside.reason: “manipulate” concerns prompt injection against the model, not persuasion of people by the model.

cells.question: Q11

passages.locator: §4 Alignment and welfare assessments, PDF p. 10
passages.quote: The alignment-related behaviors of the two models appeared to be very similar
Claude Opus 4.1 has very similar reward hacking tendencies to Claude Opus 4.

cells.note: The card reports an automated behavioural audit (including deception toward a simulated user and self-preservation), a blackmail evaluation and reward-hacking evaluations, each with a conclusion compared with Claude Opus 4.

setAside.reason: States that expert red-teaming sessions were not conducted for the RSP assessment; no red-teaming of this model is reported.

search.read: Whole card (23 pages): Introduction and §1.1, §§2–6; changelog

setAside.reason: Faculty Science, SecureBio, Deloitte Consulting and Signature Science are named as having developed evaluations; the card does not say they tested this model.
Refers to third-party assessments of Claude Opus 4 and to collaboration with external partners in general, not to testers of Claude Opus 4.1.
States that no new pre-deployment evaluations with external government partners were conducted for this release; no body is named.

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: deployed under the AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) Standard under Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) as a precautionary measure. See the Claude 4 system card for more details on this decision.

cells.note: The decision the card refers to is the ASL-3 safeguards decision made for Claude Opus 4. The card describes no decision to release Claude Opus 4.1 and names no maker for one.

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: a slight increase in indications that the model suspected that it was being evaluated—which is itself concerning, because this might reduce the validity of our assessments

cells.note: The card also states that the RSP assessment was automated only, without human uplift trials or expert red-teaming (§6.1), and that absolute audit scores should not be relied upon (Figure 4.1.A).
